evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` predicate only requires positive and changed manager PIDs plus nonempty and changed invocation IDs. It does not require the manager snapshots to share the same nonempty guest boot ID, so a guest reboot between `manager.before` and `manager.after` can satisfy it even though that is not a distinct same-boot manager restart. The separate `boot_id_changed` check is for the reboot phase and does not close this gap. Adding equal nonempty manager before/after boot IDs is a routine correctness fix for the existing check.
